title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
excerpt: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole…

ai.summary: The paper “Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long‑Horizon Agents” compares three decision‑model roles across several LLMs to see if a poorly acting model can still teach well.
ai.why: Provides insights for building better evaluation and training pipelines for long‑term autonomous agents.

title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
excerpt: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on…

ai.summary: A paper analyzes the design choices in multimodal vision encoders, arguing that they bundle a visual prior, dedicated capacity, and pre-fusion placement, and compares strategies like using pretrained encoders versus training from scratch.
ai.why: Provides architectural insights for developers building or fine-tuning multimodal LLMs who need to decide how to handle visual input encoding.

title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
excerpt: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria…

ai.summary: Researchers critique the practice of exposing benchmark success criteria to embodied agents during training, noting that these verifiers often demand more than the language instructions specify, leading to misaligned self-improvement.
ai.why: Highlights a potential flaw in current embodied AI training loops that developers should consider when designing self-improving agent systems.

title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
excerpt: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of 432 strictly paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a…

ai.summary: WorldDraft proposes separating 4D world construction from visual rendering, using multimodal coding agents to build a world and video models to render it, focusing on world preservation and visual realization.

title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
excerpt: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical…

ai.summary: PhysLoop is a framework that uses large language models' physics knowledge to guide self‑improving video generation, aiming to improve physical dynamics and causal consistency in generated videos.
ai.why: It offers a method for developers to incorporate physics reasoning into video generation pipelines.

title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
excerpt: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Test-Time Baking (TTB), a method that trains a lightweight MLP to embed global scene information from cross‑view attention of decoder‑only large view synthesis models, allowing fast high‑fidelity novel‑view rendering without full test‑time training.
ai.why: It could let developers deploy view‑synthesis models with lower latency and compute cost.

title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
excerpt: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. Prior work therefore conditions video generation on layouts that specify vehicle motion, providing control over surrounding vehicles but requiring their future trajectories as inputs. We introduce BirdDreams, an autoregressive driving world model that jointly generates perspective video and a schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, making scene layout part of the…

ai.summary: The paper 'BirdDreams' introduces a driving world model that jointly generates perspective and bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, enabling plausible simulation of surrounding vehicle motion and precise ego-trajectory control for autonomous driving research.
ai.why: Provides a new tool for simulating complex driving scenarios, which is critical for training and testing autonomous vehicle systems.

title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
excerpt: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1…

ai.summary: The paper 'Duo' introduces a Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and Duo v1, a full-duplex system that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs and responds in real-time, integrating reasoning and physical simulation into a single world model.
ai.why: Offers a new architectural approach for building interactive AI agents that can handle real-time, bidirectional communication with users.

title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
excerpt: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. Our analyses identify the design choices that matter most for generalization, including color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. These choices interact, so individually helpful choices can hurt when combined with others. Starting from 4B and…

ai.summary: Open Vision Banana (OVB) releases all data, model weights, code and implementation details to turn pretrained image generators into unified multi‑task visual perception systems.
ai.why: Provides developers with a reproducible open‑source pipeline to build perception models from existing generators.

title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
excerpt: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The…

ai.summary: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOA) is a lightweight SOAP variant that retains SOAP's convergence benefits while matching AdamW's efficiency in memory and computation.
ai.why: Developers training transformers can use FOA to speed up training without significant extra resource costs.

title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
excerpt: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. Language models have advanced along well-characterized scaling laws; the corresponding question for physical AI is how capability scales with environments and behaviors, which first requires identifying which data to scale…

title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
excerpt: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible…

ai.summary: SO-Arena is a benchmark that evaluates System One models across 11 domains, measuring both capability spectrum and decision reliability rather than just aggregate performance.

title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
excerpt: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups…

ai.summary: G-STAR proposes scaling group size quadratically with spatial compression in discrete autoregressive image models, enabling deeper compression without sacrificing token capacity.
ai.why: It provides a technique for developers to build more efficient image generation models with higher compression ratios.

title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
excerpt: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for…

ai.summary: UniSpark-9B is a 9B‑parameter multimodal model that combines full attention and GatedDeltaNet linear attention, supporting visual question answering, text‑to‑image generation, and instruction‑guided tasks.
ai.why: It demonstrates a hybrid attention architecture that could improve multimodal model efficiency for developers.

title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
excerpt: Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models, yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead. In this work, we systematically study the HC architecture to understand its components and identify simpler, more efficient designs. We find that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates form two effective interaction groups: either alone achieves performance comparable to mHC. We also identify repeated access to the expanded residual state as a major source of training overhead, even without mixing. These findings lead to SimpleHC, which simplifies the…

ai.summary: The paper studies Hyper-Connections (HC) used in large language models, showing that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates are two effective interaction groups that can match or exceed performance of more complex HC designs.
ai.why: It offers simpler, more efficient HC variants that could reduce training overhead for developers building large models.
